Time Motor Sales / Design review

One dealership. Five ways in.

Five homepage concepts · Desktop + mobile · No live transactions

Design review only · changes are not published

Search First

Direct discovery. A clear route from intent to inventory.

Recommended foundation

Premium Showroom

Photography-led. More atmosphere, fewer competing elements.

Visual polish

Guided Shopping

Preference-led discovery. Optional guidance, never a gate.

Optional shopping assistant

Signature Showroom

Your familiar local-dealership presence, modern search and a rotating vehicle showcase.

Current-site inspired

Simple Hybrid

Time Motor Sales identity, search-led simplicity and a quieter rotating showroom.

Recommended blend
Shared component system

Identity & navigation

Existing Time Motor Sales logo. Shop · Sell/Trade · Finance · Service · My Garage. Mobile uses a compact header plus Home, Shop, Saved and Garage navigation.

Action blue Quiet canvas

Typography & spacing

Arial / system sans. Desktop hero 40–48 px; mobile 34 px. Section titles 23 px; body 14–16 px; supporting labels 12 px. Spacing scale: 4 / 8 / 12 / 16 / 24 / 32 / 48. One shared corner-radius token.

Search & buttons

Visible input label, 16 px entry text, native submit button and keyboard-operable suggestions. One dominant action per section. Minimum 44 px touch targets. Selection is removable; Escape and outside click dismiss suggestions.

Vehicle cards & content

Stable photo ratio, title, trim, mileage and cash price. Save with explicit pressed state. Sample content is labeled; no invented ratings, financing approvals, discounts, delivery promises or inspection claims.

States & continuity

Search open → select → removable chip → simulated loading → result or recovery. Returning shopper is a fictional review state with saved-vehicle continuity; no real identity or private records. Guidance uses local preferences, not a live AI agent.

Accessibility & performance gates

Visible focus, labels, native controls, non-color state cues and live result announcements. No autoplay video or third-party font. Optional slides advance every six seconds, pause on hover/focus, and stop for reduced motion or hidden pages. Before adoption: screen-reader review, WCAG 2.2 AA audit and real-device speed checks. These are design targets, not certifications.

Comparison scorecard
Designer assessment of the proposed structures—not measured usability, accessibility or performance results.

Recommended: Simple Hybrid, with your showroom identity

Simple Hybrid keeps Time Motor Sales’ local identity and rotating vehicle showcase while putting search first. Signature Showroom stays closer to your current site. All five remain review options; switching concepts does not publish a homepage.
